name: ssplayer-for-react-native
description: SpriteStudio 7 player for React Native — workspace root
//scripts: Every entry point is a .js shim that picks the .sh or .ps1 implementation
for the host OS (scripts/run-platform-script.js) — naming a .sh here would
shut Windows contributors out. Same shape as SSPlayerForWeb.
check-framedata is macOS/Linux-only on purpose: it is a developer guard
that needs flatc and a host cargo build, not part of any build path.
check-mask is macOS-only for the same kind of reason: it links the host
libskia RN Skia ships, which has no Linux slice.
check-hidden needs neither flatc nor Skia — only a host cargo build — so it
is the cheapest of the three to run.
generate-fbs-code takes an optional output dir so check-framedata can
regenerate into a scratch dir and diff, rather than reimplementing it.
//overrides: npm auto-installs the package's peerDependencies at the workspace root,
which lands a second copy of each native module next to the one `expo
install` picked for example/. Two copies of a native module is not a
duplicated dependency, it is two autolinked pods/prefabs fighting over one
JSI registration. These pins collapse each one onto the version Expo's
